approach: Run the same email rule and allow-list as admission on the producer's working tree after each report, inside the producer loop. Added lines are found by comparing each changed file's new blob with its base blob (line multiset), so an address already in the base is never blamed and the scan is never stricter than admission. A hit is folded into the existing single send-back, whose text names file:line. If a hit remains after that send-back, the run fails with a reason naming file:line and the shared phrase "adds an email address outside the allow-list". The phrase is one constant in admission.rs, used by the admission message, the in-loop message and introspection. In introspection, read_records keeps each job's outcome reason. narrow_cases then also admits any earlier case whose job's outcome reason carries the admission phrase, when the new event's text carries it too. So the passed-in case list, which apply_answer checks the model's earlier_cases against, contains those cases. Add the one producer.md line, the CHANGELOG entry, and update the budget line in docs/system-facts.md.

decisions.choice: Find added lines by comparing the new blob with the old blob in the snapshot (Snapshot::change_list, Snapshot::blob). Put the pure function in athena-gate content.rs, next to disallowed_emails.
decisions.reason: Admission's Git::added_lines returns no line numbers, and athena-git is not a listed deliverable. A pure function over (old, new, allow) returns 1-based line numbers, is unit-testable, and reuses disallowed_emails and the PersonalData allow-list unchanged. Counting a line as added only when the base lacks an identical line makes it a subset of what admission flags.

decisions.choice: Match earlier cases by refusal reason in narrow_cases: add Records.job_reasons (job id to outcome reason, filled in read_records from OutcomeRow with `#[serde(default)] reason`). A case is included if class_of_work and category match, OR the event's `what` contains the admission phrase and the case's job reason does too. Keep newest-first and CASE_CAP. decisions.reason: The records the brief names are the jobs' outcomes, which already store the reason. CaseRow holds only the model's first line of what_happened, so matching on the stored outcome reason is deterministic. Once the cases are in the passed-in list, apply_answer keeps them and the model can reuse the class, so new_class is false. No CaseRow field is added, so the prompt keys that an existing test pins stay the same.

risks.risk: The in-loop scan refuses something admission would accept, so the run fails wrongly.
risks.mitigation: The scan only flags a line when its text has no identical line in the base blob, and it reuses disallowed_emails and the same allow-list. It is therefore a subset of admission's added lines. Unit tests cover the moved, duplicated, deleted, binary and allow-listed forms.

risks.risk: The signature change or new Records field breaks callers in unlisted files such as run_pin_tests.rs.
risks.mitigation: Keep send_back_text's signature and add a new function. Grep callers of send_back_text and of Records { ... } literals (Records derives Default, and Past::default() is used) before editing.

risks.risk: The prompt line pushes the producer set over 1300 tokens.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line at most about 110 bytes and run the budgets test. Update docs/system-facts.md to the computed number, never the budget.

risks.risk: A test file containing an email-like literal fails the repository's personal-data scan.
risks.mitigation: Build the test address at runtime from two parts and use an unrelated domain; the [personal_data] scan never sees an email-like literal in the source. Do not copy any address from the request into files.

risks.risk: The new match crowds out class/category cases or matches unrelated events.
risks.mitigation: Match only when both the event text and the case's job reason contain the exact EMAIL_REFUSAL phrase, still capped at CASE_CAP and newest first. A control test shows an event without the phrase is unchanged.

risks.risk: Large or binary files make the scan slow or misread.
risks.mitigation: Read blobs through Snapshot::blob only for non-deleted, non-gitlink entries, and skip any blob containing a NUL byte. Treat read failures as errors via ?, like change_list.

demonstrations.method: New test in the module produce_and_verify_order_tests of run/tests.rs. The reader and verifier use base_script(); a wrapper script for Role::Producer sets edits to README.md with a disallowed address on line 3. The address is built at runtime from two parts so no email-like literal enters the source. It then asserts the state is Failed, the reason contains 'README.md:3' and the shared phrase, the producer was invoked twice, the second user_prompt contains 'README.md:3', and no verifier ran. A unit test for the pure function in athena-gate content.rs, in the same run, checks the 1-based numbers.
demonstrations.observes: The outcome is Failed. The reason contains README.md:3 and 'adds an email address outside the allow-list'. The producer ran twice and the verifier never. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is also run: this is a producer-loop rule, not a reading or plan refusal, so it maps to no corpus case, and the run confirms the corpus is untouched.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the in-loop scan the producer runs once, the job reaches admission, and the reason is 'admission refused the change: README.md adds an email address outside the allow-list' with no ':3'. The assertions for 'README.md:3' and for two producer invocations then fail.

demonstrations.method: New tests in tests.rs. (a) The producer edits README.md to add a line with an allow-listed address (the noreply local part at a documentation domain, built at runtime); assert Landed and one producer invocation. (b) The base README is committed with a disallowed address by commit_file before ask; the producer's edit keeps that line and adds a clean one; assert Landed and one producer invocation. Unit tests in content.rs cover: no address; an allow-listed address by local part, by domain and by suffix; the same address on an unchanged line; the same address on a moved or duplicated line (the second copy is the added one); a deleted file; a binary blob with a NUL byte.

(a) Unit: Past::default() with two CaseRow with differing class_of_work and category, and Past.job_reasons holding the admission phrase for their jobs; an Event whose `what` carries the phrase; assert narrow_cases returns both newest first. A control event without the phrase returns none. (b) End to end with the existing Model and setup(): two jobs fail in the producer loop with the same address (Scenario.edits), the first answer is 'new', and a third failing job's answer chooses the class and case ids read from the prompt (like the test at lines 925-965). The end-to-end part then has an empty earlier_cases list in the prompt, apply_answer drops the model's case ids, and the record has empty earlier_cases (and new_class true if the model followed the empty list).
